bullets.title: Anthropic IPO prices at $83/share, $81.3B raised — largest listing ever, AI validation signal
bullets.body: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83/share (above expected range), raising $81.3B on 980M shares with a fully diluted valuation of ~$1.5T. Market reading the strong demand as validation of pure-play AI investment thesis; Wolfe initiates at Outperform/$135 PT projecting revenue of $53B (2026E) → $280B (2028E) on ~$11T TAM from automating knowledge work. Some caution that the stock could rally then decline 20-30% over six months as price discovery occurs.

bullets.title: S&P 500 down 5 straight sessions, -6.5% from peak; futures surge +1.3% Thursday on AI bounce
bullets.body: The S&P 500 closed below its 200-day moving average alongside the Russell 2000 and Nasdaq 100, while the 10-year yield stayed above its 50/200-day MAs — a combination seen only six times since 2008. Futures reversed sharply Thursday morning (S&P +1.29%, Nasdaq 100 +2.0%) as the Anthropic IPO and PANW blowout earnings catalyzed a broad AI/semi bid. JPM's Dubravko reiterates SPX year-end target of 8,000 (8.4% upside from current levels) with positioning at ~20th percentile offering better entry points.

bullets.title: Fed hardening: multiple officials back further hikes; December 25bp widely expected, 50bp unlikely
bullets.body: Fed rhetoric has materially stiffened — SF Fed's Daly backs additional tightening, Fed's Barr calls further hikes 'likely appropriate.' Piper, Goldman, and JPM all pencil in 25bp hikes in December, January/March, lifting the funds rate to 4.25-4.75%. JPM's 2027 outlook sees two cuts in 2028; a 50bp December move is widely dismissed as unlikely. Real 2-year yields have risen 73bp over 13 weeks, a regime historically associated with risk-asset stress.

bullets.title: Cross-asset risk monitor at 'Watch' level; equities stressed but credit/rates calm — not 2022 yet
bullets.body: The Cross-Asset Risk Monitor reads −0.68 with 19 of 34 indicators flashing, but stress is concentrated in equity volatility/correlation/beta rather than credit or rates. High-yield spreads score +0.58, loans vs T-bills +1.02 — still calm. The 2022 analog began similarly but deteriorated when credit/rates vol broke below −1.9 by March; that hasn't happened yet. All-clear signals require S&P above 7,345, IWM above $279.50, and QQQ above $682.60 simultaneously.

bullets.title: NVDA leadership vacuum weighs on stock; AMD, AVGO seen as beneficiaries of financing pullback
bullets.body: Moody's cut NVDA's credit outlook to stable from positive citing leadership vacuum and absent succession plan; the board has contacted ARM CEO Rene Haas as potential successor to Jensen Huang. NVDA is tightening vendor financing, reportedly telling neocloud partners to secure customer prepayments for GPU allocations — raising capital costs for the ecosystem. Money is flowing from NVDA into AMD and AVGO; Jefferies cut NVDA PT to $250 and JPM flagged a ~$595bn funding gap across 2027-2028 for hyperscalers as NVDA support weakens.

bullets.title: US export controls tighten: TSMC/Samsung halt China chip shipments; new license rules hit SE Asia
bullets.body: BIS issued an interim final rule requiring licenses for advanced semiconductor exports to data centers serving Country Group D:5 or Macau, and expanded controls to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. TSMC and Samsung suspended some China-bound shipments pending Commerce Department licenses. The White House is also considering additional controls on Nvidia's advanced AI chips via NDAA. Moonshot AI dropped an Indonesian Nvidia deal after US restricted remote access to advanced chips.

bullets.title: JPM $450bn AI supply forecast for 2027; $595bn funding gap warns of hyperscaler stress
bullets.body: JPM forecasts $450bn in AI-related supply for 2027 split evenly between hyperscaler bond issuance and GPU/data center financing, with aggregate FCF negative through 2028 and a base-case $595bn funding gap (downside $956bn). Capex is projected to rise from $805bn in 2026 to $1.3tr in 2027, exceeding 50% of revenue. JPM downgrades Alphabet to Neutral, retains Overweight on Amazon and Oracle, Underweight on Microsoft; S&P revised Meta's outlook to Negative (2028 leverage 1.1-1.3x).

bullets.title: AI/semi selloff may have bottomed Nov 18-19; semis, optical, and cloud infrastructure leading bounce
bullets.body: Multiple desks are calling Nov 18-19 as a potential bottom in AI/semis after a 6-week selloff. Pre-market Thursday: SMH +3.5%, DRAM +5%, neocloud infrastructure +6.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures +2.0%. Semiconductor complex (STX +6.1%, WDC +5.4%, MU +4.6%, CRDO +5.2%, ALAB +5.0%) and cloud/AI infra (CRWV +5.5%, IONQ +3.8%, SMCI +3.8%) lead. Hedge fund gross exposures are at super-low levels, meaning few are positioned to monetize a sustained bounce.

bullets.title: SaaS underperforming sharply: IGV -9.5% YTD vs S&P +10.5%; sector multiples compressing
bullets.body: The Wolfe All-SaaS index trades at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales, with the Security index at 8.1x and Vertical at 6.9x. IGV has returned -9.5% YTD against the S&P's +10.5%. Security multiples declined 7.49% week-over-week as AI displacement fears and soft CRM results keep sentiment depressed; buyside is pressing shorts in WDAY, NOW, HUBS, and CRM.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness + USD strength pressuring nominal-demand sectors; secular growers and AI infra favored
bullets.body: Implied real yields have gapped higher driven by the Fed's intent to conquer last-mile disinflation rather than additional rate hike pricing per se. The factor playbook favors Early Cyclicals and secular growers over Energy, Industrials, and Materials. Staples/Discretionary correlation at the 99th percentile on oil weakness; Bitcoin and gold are deeply negatively correlated to USD with the USD breakout acting as a commodity headwind.

bullets.title: Asia hedge funds in heavy sell mode: Taiwan/Korea AI allocations at YTD lows, L/S down MTD
bullets.body: Asia fundamental L/S managers are down 1.6% MTD in November (YTD +12.4%), with Info Tech/AI net selling running 2.4x long sales to short sales. Taiwan net allocation fell to 4.4% (24th percentile), Korea to 2.3% (11th percentile YTD low), both down from ~8% peaks in June. Asia equities net allocation dropped 260bp MTD to 24.3%, representing an 8.2% overweight vs. MSCI World, down from 20% overweight in mid-June.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley 2027 outlook: AI capex sustains 3.3% global growth; S&P 500 target 8,700
bullets.body: MS forecasts global growth of 3.3% in 2027 anchored by robust AI-related capex and wealth-supported US consumption, with S&P 500 reaching 8,700 by year-end. Inflation remains persistently elevated, with central banks in DM beginning a modest hiking cycle. China growth slows to 4.4% due to household deleveraging; UK positioned robustly with fiscal consolidation and capex growth.

bullets.title: JPM 2027 US macro: AI capex moderates, consumer slows, Fed hikes to 4.75% then cuts in 2028
bullets.body: JPM sees the AI-related spending boom peaking in 2026 with capex growth decelerating from 10% to 8% in 2027 and real consumer spending slowing from 2.6% to 1.7%. The Fed is expected to hike December, January, and March to 4.5-4.75%, then cut twice in 2028. Core PCE stays in the mid-to-high 2% range; AI is estimated to boost productivity ~0.5pp/year, though labor's income share has already declined 2.5pp to 53%.

bullets.title: GOOGL launches Gemini 4 Neon coding agent; stock +3.9% pre-market
bullets.body: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon, an AI coding agent priced at $3/M input tokens and $15/M output tokens with a 1M-token context window, scoring 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at high thinking level. The release is cited as a catalyst for the broader AI trade bounce pre-market Thursday.

bullets.title: WTI +1% to ~$83; Trump weighing Iran military strikes; two tankers hit mines in Hormuz
bullets.body: WTI crude recovered ~1% to $83.14 pre-market after falling 3%+ on Wednesday. Geopolitical risks are rising: Trump is reportedly weighing military strikes on Iran (with Iran considering bio/chemical weapons per Trump), and two tankers were hit by mines in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. Trump, Xi, and Putin separately agreed to boost refined oil supply and reiterate no nuclear war stance.

bullets.title: 10-year yield +3bps to 5.10%; BOJ expected to hike December with March follow-up pulled forward
bullets.body: The US 10-year Treasury yield ticked up to 5.10% Thursday morning, remaining above its 50 and 200-day moving averages. The Bank of Japan is expected to hike in December with a March follow-up brought forward, adding to the global tightening backdrop.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 outperforming: +0.5% Wed, +9.4% YTD; small-cap earnings tracking revenues above, EPS below
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 rose 0.5% Wednesday, outperforming the S&P 500 by 0.7%, and is now up 9.4% YTD (outperforming the S&P by 2.4%). Of the 84% of market cap that has reported 3Q26 earnings, aggregate revenues are running 1.6% above expectations while aggregate earnings track 0.4% below (6.2% below ex-financials).

bullets.title: Data center power constraints intensifying; battery supply tight through 2027, storage critical
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's SF bus tour found data center designs increasingly incorporating 6-10x solar MW relative to load with 25x battery MWh to achieve 99% uptime. Battery supply is expected to remain tight through 2027. Midterm election outcomes are expected to tighten permitting/power/water conditions for data centers rather than halt projects outright, with power as the primary constraint.

bullets.title: Global credit: modest spread widening in 2027; $440bn hyperscaler issuance + $545bn project finance ahead
bullets.body: Goldman expects modest spread widening in 2027 with AI-driven issuer dispersion as the dominant credit theme. Hyperscalers are projected to issue $440bn and project finance $545bn. Insurers currently hold only ~25% of hyperscaler bonds vs. ~45% of broad IG, leaving capacity to absorb supply, but leverage is rising (S&P cut Meta's outlook to Negative, Broadcom to Stable from Positive).

bullets.title: WMT Q3 beats across the board; eComm +23%, advertising +37%, marketplace sales +~50%
bullets.body: Walmart's Q3 adj. EPS of $0.65 beat consensus $0.64 and the top of guidance; CC adj. EBIT grew 5.5% vs guidance of 2-4%, beating consensus by ~4%. US eComm grew 23% (UBSe 25%), advertising grew 37%, and marketplace sales grew ~50%, signaling durable omnichannel momentum. CY2026 CC net sales guidance of 4.9-5.2% came in slightly below the 5.6% consensus, and adj. OI growth of 8.0-8.6% also slightly trails the 8.4% Street estimate.
